Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
316 AM EDT Sat Oct 10 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 259 AM EDT Saturday...

No big changes to this forecast package.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 259 AM EDT Saturday...

1. Drier weather through Sunday afternoon. Rainfall associated
with remnants of Isaias to bring rain to parts of our area, no
flooding expected.

2. Seasonably cool middle and end to the week with a couple 
shower chances.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 259 AM EDT Saturday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Surface high pressure builds into the region 
today, leading to mostly sunny skies, lighter winds and high 
temperatures in the 50s for most places. Relatively widespread 
frost is likely tomorrow morning, but winds are expected to 
remain brisk for a longer portion of the overnight, so extent of
frost formation in the Champlain valley is somewhat limited, 
though it could be enough for a Frost Advisory to be issued 
later. High pressure slides east Sunday and return southerly 
flow will provide warmer temperatures to rise into the 60s 
areawide. High clouds ahead of Isaias will infiltrate the region
during the afternoon Sunday. Widespread rainfall will hold off 
until after sunset for most locations with a quarter to half of 
an inch of rain expected for many locations. Areas near the 
Canadian Border will likely see the least rainfall with amounts 
closer to a tenth of an inch. Will have to monitor for heavier 
bands within the precipitation shield. This will likely change 
run to run and with the lack of mesoscale models having the 
temporal resolution to analyze this feature, we won't know about
placement of this possible banded precipitation until tomorrow 
afternoon most likely. Nevertheless, the rainfall seen Sunday 
night, even if it's in the 1-1.5 inch rain locally, will be 
highly beneficial with no flood concerns anticipated at this 
time. A strengthening mid-level jet Sunday night will help to 
quickly shift these remnants eastward with dry conditions 
expected by daybreak on Monday.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A surface low will pass through from west to east 
Tuesday night, bringing widespread showers. While it will be quick 
moving and technically more northern stream and not have a strong 
connection to Gulf/Atlantic moisture, it will include the remnants 
of Tropical Storm Rachael so there will be some efficient 
rainfall with the former tropical moisture. GEFS/EPS/CMCE 
combined probabilities of a half inch of rain range between 
30-50 percent and probabilities of an inch are below 10 percent,
so the rain would only be beneficial. Warm air aloft will 
remain on the backside so even though the cold front drops 
temperatures significantly, rainfall amounts on Sunday have 
increased slightly with most locations seeing between a quarter 
to half of an inch of rain with closer to a tenth of an inch of 
rain near the Canadian Border.ny upslope showers look to remain 
rain in the mountains. Dry, sunny and seasonably cool conditions
develop for Thursday before more shower chances arrive for 
Friday and the weekend.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Through 06Z Sunday...The trend for the rest of the night is any
lingering MVFR ceilings will scatter out by about 08Z. Afterwards,
VFR conditions will prevail in most places. The exceptions will be
MSS where there is currently fog and SLK where fog is expected to
form later in the night. This fog should continue until around
12-13Z and then lift. While a brief period of mist/fog is possible
at MPV late in the night, a prolonged episode of fog is not
expected. After the fog lifts, VFR conditions will prevail at all
terminals from the morning through the evening. Winds will generally
transition to light/variable during the rest of the night, and
remain that way through the day. Winds will transition to southerly
tonight, with gusts in the 10-20 KT range will be possible at BTV
and PBG and lighter gusts elsewhere.

Outlook...

Sunday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday Night: MVFR/IFR conditions possible. Chance SHRA.
Columbus Day: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
Monday Night: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Definite
SHRA.
Tuesday: Mainly MVFR, with areas IFR possible. Definite SHRA.
Tuesday Night: Mainly IFR, with areas MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Wednesday: Mainly MVFR, with areas IFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&
